observation: Resource rename/remove leaves stale generated files: mix ggen_igniter.sync's for_each mode:file path (lib/mix/tasks/ggen_igniter.sync.ex, for_each handling around lines 341-439) has no manifest of previously-written output paths and never deletes a file that a prior sync produced for an identity whose --out path no longer resolves (resource renamed Ticket->Case, or resource removed entirely). Real, reproduced via test/ggen_igniter_destructive_change_agent3_test.exs's 'rename resource' and 'remove resource' tests: old out_dir/ticket.ex survives on disk unchanged after the ontology no longer has a Ticket resource (rename case) or after Ticket is removed entirely.
evidence: test/ggen_igniter_destructive_change_agent3_test.exs lines ~249-320 (real mix ggen_igniter.sync subprocess runs, File.exists?(ticket_path) true after rename/remove); lib/mix/tasks/ggen_igniter.sync.ex has no orphan/prune/delete logic (grep -n 'orphan|prune|delete' returns zero matches).
blocked_on: lib/ decision: either track previously-written for_each output paths per template (a manifest file) and prune paths no longer produced by the current sync, or explicitly document this as a permanent, disclosed non-goal (mirroring the cross-file stale-reference disclosure already in test/e2e/lifecycle_test.ex's Stage 7 comments) -- Agent 3 is write-scoped to fixtures/tests only and is not patching lib/ itself.

observation: domain.ex.eex (test/fixtures/ash-lifecycle-pack/templates/domain.ex.eex) cannot correctly render a cross-domain result: its header does '<% domain_module = domain_resources |> List.first() |> Map.get("domain_module") %>' and folds ALL rows' resource(...) calls under that single first-row domain module. Once two resources resolve to two different alp:domainModule values (Ticket moved to a new alp:BillingDomain while Customer stays on alp:SupportDeskDomain), mix ggen_igniter.sync neither raises nor fans out per-domain -- it silently writes ONE file that misregisters one resource under the wrong domain module string, with no admission/validation check catching the multi-domain case before the file is written.
evidence: test/ggen_igniter_destructive_change_agent3_test.exs 'change domain association: domain.ex.eex genuinely cannot render two domains from one sync' test (lines ~378-420): real sync run against ontology_v11_change_domain_association.ttl produces exactly one defmodule folding both Ticket and Customer resource(...) calls under whichever domain_module the first 050_domain_resources.rq row carried; test/fixtures/ash-lifecycle-pack/templates/domain.ex.eex has no for_each/per-domain fan-out and no pre-write validation.
blocked_on: Either (a) give domain.ex.eex a for_each: domain_resources-style per-domain fan-out (mirrors resource.ex.eex's existing for_each: resource convention) so each distinct domain_module gets its own rendered/written file, or (b) add an admission check in lib/mix/tasks/ggen_igniter.sync.ex (or GgenIgniter.Render) that raises a clear, typed error when a non-for_each template's bound query result spans more than one distinct value for a field the template assumes is singular, refusing the write rather than silently emitting a wrong file. Agent 3 is write-scoped to fixtures/tests only and is not patching lib/ or the template itself.
